title: How a 3D Printer Works in 60 Seconds 🖨️🧱 #shorts
description:
A 3D printer builds objects one thin slice at a time. Plastic filament is fed into a heated nozzle that melts it, the nozzle traces each layer, and every new layer fuses to the one below as it cools. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#3dprinting #3dprinter #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: The first 3D printer was invented back in *1984*, and now people print *at home*.

steps.label: Filament
steps.text: A spool feeds a thin *plastic thread*, called *filament*, into the printer.

steps.label: Hot end
steps.text: A *heated nozzle* melts the plastic, like a super precise *hot glue gun*.

steps.label: Trace
steps.text: The nozzle glides around, drawing one *thin slice* of the object.

steps.label: Layers
steps.text: Then it steps up a hair and draws the *next layer* right on top.

steps.label: Fuse
steps.text: As the plastic *cools*, each layer fuses to the one below, *hundreds* of times over.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Melt, trace, *stack*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
